On The 3 rd Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 38302 of 2025
 Rahul @ Chintu
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Shashwat Seth - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Apoorv Joshi - Govt. Advocate for the respondent
 Order

1. This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.470/2025 registered at Police Station- Alot District Ratlam (M.P.)
for offence punishable under Section 420 of BNS, 2023.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 17.07.2025.

2. Heard the arguments.
3.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application,
submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the alleged offence.
It is a commercial transaction relating to the property.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
The complainant and other witnesses have been examined.
There is no likelihood 2 MCRC-38302-2025 of tampering with remaining evidence by the applicant.
The prosecution is based on documentary evidence.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant and his family members.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the trial.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel refers to 01 criminal antecedent against the applicant, as mentioned in the case diary.

sentences.text: 6. In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the other matter relating to similar offence is pending for trial.
Applicant has been extended benefit of bail.
Applicant has never been convicted.
7. According to the material available on record, Rahul Anchaliya executed an agreement to sale of a plot in favor of Babulal Porwal and Narendra Soni.
Rahul Anchaliya received Rs.5,00,000/- in cash and Rs.5,00,000/- through R.T.G.S. and promised to execute the sale deed of the plot.
Later, it was revealed that Rahul Anchaliya is not the owner of the plot and absconded with the advanced money.
The P.S. Alote registered an F.I.R. for offences punishable under Section 420 of IPC against Rahul Anchaliya.
Applicant Rahul was arrested on 16.07.2025.
He is in custody ever since.
Relevant document was seized from the possession of Rahul Anchaliya.
The final report has been submitted on completion of investigation.
The trial is under way.
Complainant Narendra Soni [PW-3] has been examined.
Other prosecution witnesses have also been examined.
The trial will take time to conclude.
The veracity of prosecution and complicity of the applicant will be determined after evidence in the trial.
As informed, the applicant is aged 36 years and he is a property broker.
He has responsibility of dependent family.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.
Considering the socio economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the remaining witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

9. Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

10. Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Rahul @ Chintu shall be released on bail in connection with Crime, as mentioned in first paragraph of this order, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/-(Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) with one surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions : (For convenience of understanding by accused and surety, the conditions of bail are also reproduced in Hindi as under):-
(1) Applicant shall remain present on every date of hearing as may be directed by the concerned court;
(1) 
  

  
 

   




 



              

 (2) Applicant shall not commit or get involved in any offence of similar nature; (2)

( 3 )
